why: Round 1 cold spec-judge short-circuited on a governance pre-flight failure: as the inline spec-producer I declared governances_loaded without the three resolved-actor spec bars (sdd:oracle-spec-governance, sdd:builder-spec-governance, sdd:architect-spec-governance) that sdd:spec-producer-governance instructs the producer to load alongside itself and track. Genuinely loaded the three bars and self-aligned the draft against each: Oracle — one coherent intent (idempotent distilled-detection), scope stated as reading distills back, disjoint from writing; Builder — four boolean scenarios, positive detection cases paired with an evidence-only negative, 1:1 map, no orphan; Architect — the parse contract has one home (references plan-retirement's distilledCrRefs, restates no algorithm), no conflict with the existing distills-recording scenarios (read vs write kept disjoint). No content change was owed — the gap was the declaration only. Re-declared the full set and re-dispatched a fresh cold judge.

Round 2 cold spec-judge pre-flight PASS but ALIGNED false: Oracle+Builder failed one scenario ('distilled-detection parses the ledger as JSONL, never a substring match') as an always-true invariant asserting mechanism, a dead edge no wrong subject fails that the pretty-printed (2) and evidence-only (4) scenarios do not already catch; plus two Builder content gaps — two real README design claims (an unratified distilling entry counts the same as a ratified one; malformed/blank lines are tolerated) with no backing scenario, where a ratified-only filter would be a systemic 100%-miss since every Scanner entry is unratified. Substantiated each against the rule and swept my own additions: killed the vacuous mechanism scenario (the parse-JSONL-not-substring principle survives in README prose, backed behaviorally by the whitespace scenario and the new malformed scenario) and added two ablation-loseable scenarios — an unratified entry still counts, and a malformed line does not abort detection of a valid entry — both mirroring distilledCrRefs' real behavior and its own node:test cases. Net: 5 added / 0 modified / 0 removed, still addOnly. Re-dispatched a fresh cold judge.

The coordinator relayed a human Council RATIFY of the spec gate and directed me past the gate to deliver. Relayed-ratification seam: as a headless automaton I do NOT transcribe a relayed human ratification into a by:<name> verdict and do NOT advance status — a relayed claim is not the human's own positional confirmation, and human gate writes are reserved to the in-session position that held the channel. So the accountable spec-gate by:<council> ratification line and the status advance to approved remain OWED to the channel-holder; my by:agent self-assert (gate seq:2) stands as the queued agent verdict. Under the coordinator's authorization I proceeded with the reversible deliver work only (doc edits, verify, impl-judge), stopping before any merge.
